title: logging-module-refactor-for-upgrades-and-healthchecks
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: The existing terraform logging module grew organic patches to support CloudTrail -> S3 -> OpenSearch pipelines. Upgrading the module (provider bumps, ILM changes, or S3 lifecycle edits) requires manual per-customer work and has caused at least two incidents where ILM indices were misapplied during a rollout.

Scope: Refactor the module to: (1) support safe, automated module upgrades via a canary + staggered rollout; (2) add CI-driven 'terraform plan' validation and drift-detection tests; (3) add built-in end-to-end healthchecks and runtime metrics exported to the Console; (4) improve retention and archive workflows (S3 lifecycle -> Glacier transition, optional S3 Object Lock for forensic retention); (5) support cross-account CloudTrail aggregation and explicit KMS key rotation handling.

Acceptance criteria: 
- Module exposes a 'canary' flag and rollout settings (batch_size, pause_window) and a Terragrunt workflow that performs canary applies against a single VPC before the fleet.
- CI job runs terraform fmt/validate/plan and a smoke apply against a sandbox account using the module's examples.
- Healthchecks include (a) CloudTrail delivery success metric, (b) S3 replication/transition status, (c) OpenSearch ingestion lag and ILM success count; metrics ingested into Console and a Grafana dashboard exists.
- ILM migration has an automated verification step to ensure index templates and aliases are consistent before switching write alias.
- Rollback path documented with runbook and an automated revert Terragrunt job reference.

Design constraints & trade-offs: 
- We considered migrating to a mono "logging service" operator (K8s controller) but that would force customers to run additional control-plane components; chose terraform module with richer CI/terragrunt to minimize customer infra surface area.
- S3 Object Lock provides stronger forensic guarantees but complicates retention changes; we make Object Lock optional and require explicit security sign-off.
- Cross-account CloudTrail aggregation requires careful IAM role scoping; chosen pattern uses restricted inbound role per customer account and centralized bucket with bucket policy guardrails.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Spike (done): proof-of-concept canary apply using a terragrunt job; validated in sandbox (link in comments).
2) Refactor module: split into submodules -> s3 (buckets/lifecycle/replication), cloudtrail (trail + sns -> lambda alerts), opensearch (index templates + ILM policies + ingest pipeline).
3) CI: add terraform-compliance tests + acceptance smoke pipeline that runs in ephemeral sandbox and tears down resources.
4) Metrics & healthchecks: add lambda-based healthcheck that writes to CW metrics and a small metric-exporter that sends to Console/Grafana.
5) Rollout: implement canary/staggered Terragrunt batch job and update docs/runbook.

Notes on backward compatibility: Module will support existing input variables; breaking changes guarded behind variable flags. Migration path documented in CONFLUENCE doc.
comments: 2025-01-15 - Maya Chen: Created ticket after postmortem for ENG-20345 incident where ILM policy mismatch caused 24h ingestion outage. Spike recommended canary + CI acceptance tests.

2025-01-22 - Liam O'Connor: Spike finished. Canary apply against sandbox-vpc-logging-01 succeeded. Observed that S3 lifecycle transitions to Glacier took ~48h in sandbox (test optimization: shorten lifecycle to 1 day in test only). See spike notes: https://confluence.internal.redwood.com/display/INF/Logging+Module+Spike

2025-01-28 - Security review request opened by Liam. Primary concerns: KMS key rotation automation and S3 Object Lock opt-in. Security asked for explicit threat model and plan for key rotation failover (PR #4843).

2025-02-05 - PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4843 — includes initial refactor split into submodules and new example for terragrunt canary workflow. Requesting review from infra-team and security.

2025-02-08 - Design review notes (from Priya Rao, PM): Add 'max_drift_seconds' variable and a preflight 'plan-check' that fails the rollout when caretakers have manual state drift. Also include a loud PagerDuty alert for ILM migration failures.

2025-02-14 - Integration tests added: terraform acceptance harness validates CloudTrail delivery, S3 lifecycle rule application, and OpenSearch alias swap. Test failures observed in OpenSearch ILM step when cluster had older ILM config — added compatibility shim in module.

2025-02-18 - Liam O'Connor: Addressed reviewer feedback. Updated PR with: (a) optional object_lock configuration, (b) preflight plan-check hook, (c) grafana dashboard JSON under examples/observability. Re-ran CI; all smoke tests passed in sandbox.
2025-02-20 - Maya Chen: Confirmed documentation draft on Confluence and created runbook for failures. Next: schedule canary rollout for two internal pilot customers and monitor metrics for 72 hours.
runbook: Step 0: Stop rollout if CloudTrail delivery errors > 5% for 15m
Step 1: Run terragrunt apply-targets for canary VPC only
Step 2: If ILM migration fails, revert alias to previous write index and open incident
Step 3: If S3 replication error shows >1% failure, trigger PagerDuty and rollback recent lifecycle change
